indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of the two words are performed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A well-to-do man called Richard performs on some musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' is the anagram signal: the letters of POSH RICHARD are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard whose strings are plucked is a classic musical instrument.

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, a British detective branch

explanation.surface: A squad of detectives is said to be keen-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in taste means sour or tart, as an acidic substance is.

definitions.meaning: vulgar in its old sense means of the common people
liked by many people

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that being well-liked is merely common.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the Latin for the people: belonging to ordinary folk, and liked by many.

clue.text: I almost take a chance with her

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to take a chance is to risk

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of gambling on a romance with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter, K, from RISK to leave RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female name, so a pronoun for a woman stands for it.

clue.text: At end of quarrel, one may be buried

definitions.text: At end of quarrel, one may be buried

parts.words: At end of quarrel, one may be buried
parts.note: alludes to the idiom of burying a weapon to signal a quarrel is over

explanation.surface: Grim talk of a body being buried after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'bury the hatchet' means to make peace after a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for ending a feud is to bury this small axe.

definitions.meaning: past participle of to ring, to call by phone
a noun: a crossbar or step on a ladder

explanation.surface: Someone made a phone call and talked.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of ring means called by phone; as a noun it is a ladder step, a kind of spoke.

clue.text: See a bit of fluff, but don't whistle? Strange

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the words are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to spot a floating fluff but not to whistle at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' is the anagram signal over DONT WHISTLE; the apostrophe gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The downy seeds of a thistle float about as wisps of fluff.

clue.text: Ugly person could not make such a picture

definitions.text: Ugly person could not make such a picture

parts.words: Ugly person could not make such a picture
parts.note: plays on the phrase used of a plain person, that they are 'no' such canvas artwork

explanation.surface: An unattractive person is unable to produce a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: An unattractive person is said to be 'no oil painting'; the clue reads this as being unable to make one.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas worked in oils is a kind of picture, and plain people are said to be no such thing.

clue.text: Girl goes to bank office with peace offering

parts.note: Olive is a girl's name
a local office of a bank is a branch

explanation.surface: A young woman visits her local bank, bearing a gift to make up.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig from the olive tree is the traditional symbol of a peace gesture.

parts.note: bugging read as infecting with bugs, that is microbes, rather than spying

explanation.surface: Planting listening devices on an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugging' suggests eavesdropping, but here bugs are germs used as weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Biological warfare uses microbes to sicken an opposing army.

clue.text: One of four who are relatively old

definitions.text: One of four who are relatively old

parts.words: One of four who are relatively old
parts.note: relatively means as relatives; everyone has four such elders

explanation.surface: One member of a quartet who are fairly elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' means 'as relatives', not 'fairly': each person has four of these older kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person has two pairs of elders a generation above their parents, four relatives in all.

definitions.meaning: to keep back or book
the cargo area of a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone sets aside an area for storing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back is to retain it; a ship's cargo compartment shares the word.

definitions.meaning: equipment or clothing for an activity
a motorist shifts between these ratios of a gearbox

explanation.surface: Equipment swapped around by a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is called this informally, and a motorist shifts the transmission setting of the same name.

parts.note: to sever is to break off
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A handful of people split up with a young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning more than two but not many, it stands for a small number.

definitions.meaning: to run off fast, an informal phrase
legitimate drama, as opposed to musicals or variety

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to see a serious play.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away quickly is informal slang; the same letters are short for legitimate drama.

clue.text: Is he the most attractive person at the wedding

definitions.text: Is he the most attractive person at the wedding

parts.words: Is he the most attractive person at the wedding
parts.note: reads the groom's supporter as literally the finest man present

explanation.surface: A guest wonders who is the best-looking person at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of the groom's chief attendant is read literally as 'the finest man'.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom's chief supporter at a wedding carries this title, read here as the finest fellow.

clue.text: Roars out expression of disgust over writing

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: boo is a jeer showing disapproval
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone bellows out a jeer at a written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts BOO above MS.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep resounding noise, as of guns or thunder, is a roar.

clue.text: Salesman returns to put plant in bigger container

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: returns means the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman comes back to move a plant into a larger pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns TO into OT, which follows REP.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a plant into a new, usually larger pot is the gardening sense.

parts.note: L stands for pound, the British unit of money
OBs is short for outside broadcasts, programmes made away from the studio

explanation.surface: Someone tosses cash at television crews filming on location.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss something in a high arc is a kind of throw.

definitions.meaning: affected and exaggerated in manner
a group or faction holding shared views

explanation.surface: A gathering of stage folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated, showy behaviour is called this; a faction or side in a dispute shares the word.

clue.text: Letter from abroad for US soldiers returning to Massachusetts

indicators.note: returning means the word for the soldiers is read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A letter from overseas for American troops going home to New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GIS into SIG, then MA follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek character, so a letter from a foreign alphabet.

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of the word could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something is harsher when done backwards, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the anagram fodder, with 'perhaps' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of severe, meaning harsher or sterner.

parts.note: tumbling read as gymnastic tumbling, the way the performer earns, not money falling

explanation.surface: A man watches his earnings collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbling' suggests falling wages, but it is the circus act that earns him a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus gymnast earns money from tumbling and other feats.

indicators.note: release from suggests the letters are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is granted their freedom after being caught in a police sweep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release from' is the anagram signal on GRANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic police operation to catch suspects, named after a trawling net.

clue.text: He makes fun of one eating fast

definitions.meaning: one who mocks or jeers
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A mocker who gobbles food.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocker is called this, and in British slang to scoff is also to wolf food down.

definitions.meaning: a town in Caithness, far north Scotland
the cord in a lamp sits in oil

explanation.surface: A Scottish town hemmed in by the oil industry.
explanation.walkthrough: WICK is a town in the far north of Scotland; the second sense is a lamp's cord standing in fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caithness town shares its name with the cord of an oil lamp, which sits in the fuel.

definitions.meaning: to wail in lament for the dead
eager to do something

explanation.surface: Someone wails out of worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail over the dead is an Irish lament; as an adjective the word means eager.

clue.text: Make clothes perhaps-stuff must have name in

indicators.note: in tells us the name letter goes inside the word for stuff

parts.note: kit is gear or belongings, stuff

explanation.surface: Making clothes requires stuff with a name label sewn in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside KIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting with yarn and needles is one way to make garments.

clue.text: Ireland's hesitation before return of Ulster

indicators.note: before places the hesitation ahead of the next piece

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: return of means the abbreviation for Ulster is read backwards

parts.note: NI stands for Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: Ireland pauses before Ulster comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'return of' turns NI into IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic old name for the country, from Irish Éire.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: to feed is to dine

explanation.surface: Someone fattens a certain woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female name, so a woman can stand for it.

clue.text: Skeleton of fish may be put on cloth

definitions.meaning: the bony frame of a common oily fish
a zigzag weave pattern used in fabric

explanation.surface: A fish's bones might be laid on a tablecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones of an Atlantic fish give their name to a zigzag weave seen in tweed.

clue.text: Intrigued at deplorable failure to show proper appreciation

indicators.note: deplorable suggests the letters are in a sorry state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is curious about a shameful lack of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deplorable' is the anagram signal on INTRIGUED AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Not being thankful is being unthankful.
